title: Knowledge check: State-Driven Animation and Motion Design

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “State-Driven Animation and Motion Design”?
options: Scoped styles automatically affect every unrelated component.
List movement can be animated reliably without stable identity.
Use CSS or Vue transitions to communicate a real state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
Animation should be the only signal for errors.
questions.answer_key: Use CSS or Vue transitions to communicate a real state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses State-Driven Animation and Motion Design directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “CSS transitions and keyframes”, which practice is most reliable?
options: List movement can be animated reliably without stable identity.
Use CSS or Vue transitions to communicate a real state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
Animation should be the only signal for errors.
Scoped styles automatically affect every unrelated component.
questions.answer_key: Use CSS or Vue transitions to communicate a real state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “CSS transitions and keyframes”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “State-Driven Animation and Motion Design” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
